questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of Kubernetes security basics (SecurityContext, volumes, network policies) and practical CI integration for early feedback.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes SecurityContext and container privileges
- Volume types (hostPath) and their risks
- NetworkPolicy for egress control
- CI gates (GitHub Actions) and local verification with kind/kubectl

## Code Example

```yaml
name: k8s-security-gate
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Validate manifests
        run: |
          kubectl version --client
          kubeval manifests/*.yaml
          bash scripts/validate.sh
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
violations=0
for f in manifests/*.yaml; do
  if grep -qE "hostPath|runAsNonRoot|NetworkPolicy" "$f"; then :; else echo "General policy missing in $f"; violations=$((violations+1)); fi
  # pseudo-checks for brevity; real checks parse YAML (e.g., yq)
done
if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then exit 1; fi
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend the gate for multi-namespace environments?
- Which tool would you use to auto-fix non-compliant manifests, if any?

## Why This Is Asked
Demonstrates practicalPolicy as code design with Gatekeeper/OPA, multi-cloud awareness, and enforcing both pod and network baselines.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper/OPA policy authoring and constraint templates
- Pod Security Standards implications (non-root, readOnlyRootFilesystem, privileged escalation)
- Per-namespace NetworkPolicy enforcement and centralized egress allowlist
- Local validation and CI integration (dry-run, audits)

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (K8sSecurityBaseline)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8securitybaseline
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sSecurityBaseline
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8securitybaseline
      violation["RunAsNonRoot"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true }
      violation["ReadOnlyRoot"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true }
      violation["NoNETAdmin"] { input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.capabilities.NET_ADMIN == true }
```
```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sSecurityBaseline
metadata:
  name: require-baseline
spec:
  match:
   Kinds:
    - apiGroups: ["apps"]
      kinds: ["Deployment"]
```

- How would you exempt specific namespaces or workloads without weakening overall policy?
- How would you test policy drift and maintain allowlists across clouds?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-world multi-tenant data platforms require strong admission control to enforce image provenance and host security postures across clouds. Gatekeeper with Rego enables centralized policy with testable manifests.

## Key Concepts
- Open Policy Agent Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint objects
- Image provenance: registry, non-latest, digest
- Pod hardening: resources, securityContext, privilegeEscalation
- Namespace labeling and admission scope
- CI validation: conftest, gatekeeper audit, sample manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (ImageProvenanceAndSecurity)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: imageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package imageprovenance
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          some i
          container := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i]
          image := container.image
          startswith(image, "registry.example.com/")
          not endswith(image, ":latest")
          some digest := input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[i].imageDigest
          msg := "image must be from registry.example.com with digest"
        }
```
```yaml
# Constraint (ImageProvenanceConstraint)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ImageProvenanceConstraint
metadata:
  name: require-provenance
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest: unsigned or latest, missing resources
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: data
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: proc
        image: registry.example.com/data/processor:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest: compliant image, resources, and securityContext
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: data
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: proc
        image: registry.example.com/data/processor@sha256:abcdef...
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

- How would you test policy changes locally before applying to cluster?
- How would you roll out a breaking policy change across multiple namespaces without downtime?

```yaml
name: cosign-gate

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of simple security defaults in Kubernetes and CI gates that prevent risky deployments.

## Key Concepts
- NetworkPolicy basics: default-deny, ingress/egress rules
- CI gate that scans manifests across namespaces
- Local + CI validation workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
# .github/workflows/netpol-gate.yml
name: NetPol Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  netpol-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v3
        with:
          version: 'latest'
      - run: kubectl version --client
      - run: |
          for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
            kubectl -n $ns get networkpolicy >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Missing NP in $ns"; exit 1; }
          done
```

```yaml
# examples/fail/no-netpol.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: example
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
```

```yaml
# examples/pass/default-deny.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
  ingress: []
  egress: []
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this gate to auto-create the default-deny NP if missing?
- How would you adapt for namespaces created by a gateway or CI namespace isolation?

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses practical runtime policy design for multi-tenant clusters, evaluating the candidate's understanding of privilege control and secure storage isolation in production environments.

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests ability to translate governance requirements into concrete, enforceable policies and CI steps. 
- Combines data catalog metadata with image provenance and basic security gates in a beginner-friendly way.

Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper)
- Annotations for data governance (data-catalog.uri)
- Image provenance (digest pinning, registry allowlist)
- Basic hardening (forbidden hostNetwork/hostPath, non-privileged)
- Namespace quotas and network policies

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: governance-baseline
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-data-catalog
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "data.catalog.uri annotation required"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            data.catalog.uri: "?*"
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "image must be pinned with digest"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: "*@sha256:*"
  - name: disallow-risky-fields
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod", "Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    prune: false
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork/hostPath/privileged not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: False
        volumes: []
```

Failing Manifest (example)
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: team-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      hostNetwork: true
      volumes:
        - name: data
          hostPath:
            path: /data
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry.internal/data-processor:latest
```

Passing Manifest (example)
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: data-processor
  namespace: team-a
  annotations:
    data.catalog.uri: "https://catalog.example.org/datasets/123"
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry.internal/data-processor@sha256:abcdef123456...
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "128Mi"
              limits:
              cpu: "200m"
              memory: "256Mi"
```

- How to handle exceptions per-namespace while preserving governance?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CI policy enforcement skills using image signing—a common real-world requirement in production Kubernetes environments. It assesses understanding of supply chain security and GitOps practices.

## Key Concepts
- Container image signing with cosign
- Public key infrastructure for signature verification

## Code Example

**GitHub Actions Workflow:**
```yaml
name: Verify Image Signatures
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - 'manifests/**'

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Extract image references
        id: images
        run: |
          echo "images=$(grep -roh 'registry.example.com/[^"]+' manifests/ | sort -u | jq -R -s -c '. | split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          for image in $(echo '${{ steps.images.outputs.images }}' | jq -r '.[]'); do
            cosign verify --key cosign.pub $image
          done
```

**Sample Manifest (signed image):**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: myapp
        image: registry.example.com/myapp:v1.0.0
```

**Failing Manifest (unsigned):**
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: myapp
        image: registry.example.com/myapp:unsigned
```


## Why This Question Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to integrate image provenance with runtime governance in a GPU-driven, multi-tenant Kubernetes environment. It spans CI pipelines, admission controls, and cross-system attestations—core skills for securing production ML platforms.

## Key Concepts
- **Image Provenance**: Using cosign and Rekor to cryptographically verify container image origins
- **SBOM Signing and Verification**: Ensuring software bills of materials are tamper-proof and traceable
- **Central Provenance Store**: A single source of truth for validated digest information
- **Admission Constraints**: Kyverno/OPA policies enforcing GPU type and quota at deploy time

## Code Example
```yaml
# GitHub Actions: Sign, generate SBOM, and attest
name: Gate: image provenance
on: [push]
env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
  SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.COSIGN_KEY }}

jobs:
  build-sign-attest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3
      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Generate and sign SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json=sbom.json
          cosign attest --yes --key ${{ env.SIGNING_KEY }} \
            --type sbom \
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
      - name: Upload to Rekor (automatic with cosign attest)
        run: |
          echo "Rekor entry created automatically during attestation"
      - name: Store central provenance digest
        run: |
          DIGEST=$(docker inspect ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}')
          echo "${{ github.sha }}:$DIGEST" >> provenance_store.txt
```

```yaml
# Kyverno admission policy
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-gate
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-image-digest
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      verifyImages:
        - imageReferences:
            - "ghcr.io/*"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keyless:
                    subject: "https://github.com/org/*"
                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
          verifyDigest: true
          required: true
    - name: enforce-gpu-type
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      context:
        - name: namespace
          apiCall:
            urlPath: /api/v1/namespaces/{{ request.namespace }}
      preconditions:
        - key: "{{ request.namespace }}"
          operator: NotEquals
          value: "kube-system"
      validate:
        message: "GPU type must match namespace label"
        pattern:
          spec:
            template:
              spec:
                containers:
                  - (resources.limits."nvidia.com/gpu"): "?*"
    - name: enforce-gpu-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Deployment]
      validate:
        message: "GPU quota exceeded for namespace"
        deny: |
          {{ exists request.namespace.metadata.labels."gpu-quota" }}
```

## Verification Steps

**Local verification:**
```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type sbom --key pub.key ghcr.io/org/ml-platform@sha256:abc123

# Check Rekor transparency log
rekor-cli get --uuid <rekor-uuid>
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to translate security requirements into policy-as-code and integrate it into CI/CD with runtime enforcement.

## Key Concepts
- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Rego policy
- Pod security primitives: hostNetwork, hostPID, privileged, runAsNonRoot
- CI validation: gatekeeper-audit or dashboard checks, and runtime admission

## Code Example
```rego
package gatekeeper.k8spriv
violation[{"msg":"privileged containers not allowed"}] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
  some i
  container := input.review.object.spec.containers[i]
  container.securityContext.privileged == true
}
violation[{"msg":"disallow hostNetwork"}] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
  input.review.object.spec.hostNetwork == true
}
violation[{"msg":"disallow hostPID"}] {
  input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
  input.review.object.spec.hostPID == true
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this to cover initContainers?
- How would you test edge cases like multi-container pods with mixed securityContexts?
